breakdown: No transfer tax or stamp duty; registry fee 50-200 GEL, notary under 0.1%, legal 0.5-1%; agent 2-3% if buyer-paid.
annual_property_tax: Only for tax residents: 0.05-1% of value depending on household income; non-residents generally exempt.
rental_income_tax: 5% of gross rent on residential property (long- or short-term), residents and non-residents alike.

breakdown: Notary 0.23-0.35% + lawyer 0.1-0.5% + agent 1-2%; transfer tax (0.5-3%) is paid by the seller (GPG, 2021).
annual_property_tax: Local property tax ~0.05% of cadastral value (about EUR 75/yr on EUR 150k).
rental_income_tax: Flat 15% on rental income, including short-term, declared via the DIVA platform.

breakdown: Registration fee on the deed (tinglysningsafgift) of DKK 1,850 plus 0.6% of the price, about 1% for a buyer's lawyer, and, if you borrow, a mortgage registration fee of DKK 1,825 plus 1.25% of the loan; the seller normally pays the agent.
annual_property_tax: Owners pay property value tax (ejendomsværdiskat) of 0.51% on 80% of the official valuation (1.4% above DKK 9.2 million) plus municipal land tax (grundskyld) at a rate set by each municipality, capped at 30 per mille of the land value.
rental_income_tax: A non-resident who rents out a Danish home is taxed in Denmark on the profit under the ordinary Danish rules; staying in Denmark more than 3 months at a time or 180 days a year, or working there, makes you fully tax liable.

breakdown: New build: 21% VAT is normally included in the developer price, buyer pays notary + ~1% legal; resale: 3% transfer tax (progressive on higher values) + notary + ~1% legal (GPG 4.01%).
annual_property_tax: Municipal, ~0.25-1% of assessed value (higher rates possible for tourist properties).
rental_income_tax: Around 15% withholding for non-residents.

breakdown: Stamp duty on the title (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price or tax value, whichever is higher, plus a SEK 825 fee; if you borrow and need new mortgage deeds (pantbrev), 2% of their amount plus a SEK 375 fee; optional legal advice; the seller normally pays the agent, and a cooperative flat (bostadsrätt) has no lagfart.
annual_property_tax: Houses pay a municipal property fee (kommunal fastighetsavgift) of SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.
rental_income_tax: Non-resident individuals pay 30% tax on net rental income as capital income; for a private home you can first deduct SEK 40,000 per property and 20% of the rent (the 20% does not apply to a bostadsrätt).

breakdown: Buyers usually pay provincial land transfer tax on a sliding scale (Ontario: 0.5% up to $55,000 and 1% from $55,000 to $250,000), legal fees of about $500 to $1,500, title insurance of about $250 and an inspection of $300 to $1,000, while the seller usually pays the agents; foreign buyers also pay Ontario's 25% non-resident speculation tax anywhere in Ontario and British Columbia's 20% additional tax in Metro Vancouver and four other regions.
annual_property_tax: Property tax is set by each city as a share of assessed value, from about 0.3% in Vancouver to 2.12% in Saint John in 2026.
rental_income_tax: Non-residents have 25% of gross rent withheld, but they can file a Section 216 return to pay tax on net rent instead, and Form NR6 lets the agent withhold on net rent.

breakdown: Document duty (dokumentavgift) of 2.5% of market value, a registration fee (tinglysingsgebyr) of NOK 545 for the deed and NOK 545 for any mortgage document; a flat in a housing cooperative (borettslag) has no document duty; the seller normally pays the agent.
annual_property_tax: Some municipalities charge property tax (eiendomsskatt), at most 4 per mille of the value after a reduction of at least 30%, and some also give a basic deduction; many charge nothing.
rental_income_tax: Rental profit is normally taxed at 22%, and the Tax Administration says its rental rules also apply to owners who are tax resident abroad.

breakdown: New developer apartment: 10% VAT usually already in the price + 0.5% registration fee + 2% maintenance fund + notary/admin; GPG lists 2.55-3.1% buyer costs.
annual_property_tax: Non-agricultural land-use tax 0.03-0.15% of state land value; negligible for apartments.
rental_income_tax: 10% of gross rent (5% VAT + 5% PIT) above the exemption threshold; threshold raised to VND 1 billion/yr from 1 Jan 2026 (older guides say VND 100 million).

breakdown: Land Registry transfer fees of 3% up to €85,000, 5% to €170,000 and 8% above, halved for resales without VAT (1.5%, 2.5% and 4%); stamp duty abolished from 1 January 2026; lawyer about 1% plus VAT; small Land Registry charges.
annual_property_tax: There is no annual national property tax (abolished in 2017); owners pay municipal fees of about €90 to €300 a year, plus sewerage and local authority charges.
rental_income_tax: Non-residents pay income tax on Cyprus rental income at 20% to 35% after deducting 20% of the gross rent and loan interest, plus a 2.65% health contribution (GHS); the special defence contribution does not apply to them.

breakdown: Stamp duty of 1% of the price up to €1 million (2% from €1 million to €1.5 million and 6% above), solicitor's fees of about 1-1.5% plus 23% VAT, and registration fees of €425 to €800; the seller pays the estate agent, whose fee is usually built into the asking price.
annual_property_tax: Local Property Tax (LPT): from 2026 a home valued up to €240,000 pays a basic €95 a year and one valued €240,001 to €315,000 pays €235; each council can raise or lower the basic rate by up to 15%, and most raised it by 15% for 2026.

breakdown: Transfer tax (Handänderungssteuer, droits de mutation) 0% to about 3.3% depending on the canton; notary about 0.1-0.5%; land register fee, a small fixed amount or percentage; optional lawyer 1-2%; the agent fee (2-3%) is paid by the seller.
annual_property_tax: More than half of the cantons charge an annual property tax (Liegenschaftssteuer), usually 0.01-0.3% of the assessed value, and owners also pay cantonal wealth tax on the property value minus the mortgage.
rental_income_tax: Non-residents pay tax on net Swiss rental income at ordinary cantonal and communal rates plus federal direct tax, and some cantons set the rate using worldwide income.

breakdown: Tax on civil law transactions (PCC) 2% of the value, paid by the buyer within 14 days of the deed; notary fee (taksa notarialna) capped at PLN 1,010 plus 0.4% of the value above PLN 60,000, plus 23% VAT; court fee of PLN 200 to enter ownership in the land register (plus PLN 100 for a new register); optional lawyer about 1%; the agent fee (about 2-3%) depends on the agreement.
annual_property_tax: Owners pay a local property tax (podatek od nieruchomości) set by the commune, capped in 2026 at PLN 1.25 per m² of usable floor space for flats and houses.
rental_income_tax: Private rental income is taxed as a flat lump sum (ryczałt) of 8.5% of revenue up to PLN 100,000 a year and 12.5% above that.

breakdown: Closing costs vary by state and typically run 2-5% of the loan amount, covering title search and title insurance, recording fees, attorney fees, appraisal and lender fees; since August 2024 the seller no longer has to pay the buyer's agent, so the buyer may pay it unless the seller agrees to; FIRPTA does not apply when you buy but does when a foreigner later sells, with the buyer generally withholding 15% of the sale price.
annual_property_tax: Property tax is set locally and in 2024 averaged about 1.22% of value across the largest city in each state, from 0.30% in Honolulu to 3.02% in Detroit.
rental_income_tax: By default a non-resident pays 30% of gross rent (or a lower treaty rate), withheld at source, or can elect to treat the rent as business income and pay graduated rates on net income by filing Form 1040-NR and giving Form W-8ECI to the withholding agent.

breakdown: Transfer tax (overdrachtsbelasting) of 8% if you will not live in the home, such as a buy-to-let or holiday home, or 2% if it becomes your main home; a notary fee for the transfer deed of around EUR 500; Kadaster registration fees; and mortgage costs if you borrow; the seller pays its own agent.
annual_property_tax: Owners pay municipal property tax (onroerendezaakbelasting, OZB) on the official WOZ value, at a rate each municipality sets, which in practice is a per mille figure; tenants of homes do not pay it.
rental_income_tax: Non-residents declare Dutch property in box 3, where tax is 36% on a deemed return of 6% of the property's value in 2026, after a tax-free allowance of EUR 59,357 per person, regardless of actual rent.

breakdown: The buyer pays a 3% transfer tax (0% for qualifying first purchases under CONFOTUR tourism incentives), legal fees of about 1-2% and notary fees of about 0.25-1%, plus registration costs, while the seller pays the 2-3% agent fee.
annual_property_tax: The yearly IPI tax is 1% of the part of a person's total Dominican property value, as assessed by the tax office DGII, above RD$10,695,494 in 2026, so a single cheap home is often below the threshold.
rental_income_tax: Rent paid abroad to a non-resident is generally subject to 27% withholding.

breakdown: Acquisition tax 2-5% + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-1.5% (GPG 3.5-7.5%), plus 0.5-1.5% for fideicomiso/permit setup; TheLatinvestor budgets 5-8%.
annual_property_tax: Municipal predial, set locally on cadastral value; usually small, often less than HOA fees.
rental_income_tax: Non-residents: 25% ISR withholding on gross rent; plus 16% IVA on short-term stays (Airbnb remits on its bookings).

breakdown: Transfer tax 0.1-3% (municipal; Sofia 2.5%) + notary 0.1-1.5% + legal 0.5-1% + agent 2.5-3%.
annual_property_tax: 0.01-0.45% of the property's tax value plus a municipal garbage fee.
rental_income_tax: Non-residents: 10% final tax on gross rent, paid quarterly, no deductions.

breakdown: In England and Northern Ireland, Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) is 0% up to £125,000 and 2% from £125,001 to £250,000, plus a 2% surcharge for non-UK residents and a further 5% if you already own a home anywhere, so a non-resident who owns another home pays 7% up to £125,000 and 9% to £250,000; solicitor (conveyancer) about 0.6-1% with a typical minimum of around £2,100 including VAT; Land Registry fee £20 to £230; searches extra; the seller pays the estate agent.
annual_property_tax: Owners or occupiers pay council tax to the local council, and many councils in England charge second homes a premium of up to 100% from April 2025.
rental_income_tax: Non-resident landlords pay UK income tax on rent at 20%, 40% or 45%, with 20% deducted at source by the agent or tenant unless HMRC approves gross payment, and the rates on property income are set to rise to 22%, 42% and 47% from April 2027.

breakdown: Transfer tax 3.09% of the price or the taxable value, whichever is higher; notary about 0.8-1% plus VAT; land registry fees about 0.5-0.7%; lawyer 1-2% plus VAT; if an agent is used, the buyer usually pays a commission of 1-3% plus VAT on top.
annual_property_tax: Owners on 1 January pay the unified property tax (ENFIA), calculated per property from its location, size, age and official zone value, with an extra charge if total Greek property exceeds €500,000.
rental_income_tax: Non-residents pay Greek tax on Greek rental income at 15% up to €12,000, 25% to €24,000, 35% to €36,000 and 45% above, after a flat 5% deduction for expenses.

breakdown: Transfer tax (ITP) of 2% for the buyer and 2% for the seller, on the cadastral value (valor real) set by the Dirección Nacional de Catastro; notary fees of about 3%; and an agent's fee of about 3%.

Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) of 3.5% to 6.5% depending on the state (3.5% in Bavaria, 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein), plus notary and land registry fees (Notar- und Grundbuchkosten) of about 1.5-2%; if the seller hired the agent, the buyer pays half the commission by law, which is extra.
annual_property_tax: Owners pay property tax (Grundsteuer), calculated since 2025 as assessed value x a tax rate x a municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) that each municipality sets.
rental_income_tax: Non-resident owners are taxed in Germany on net rental income at the normal progressive income tax rates, but without the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag).

breakdown: The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.
annual_property_tax: Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.
rental_income_tax: Rent paid to a non-resident is subject to 20.42% withholding (except when an individual rents it as their own home), and the owner must file a tax return each year through a tax representative in Japan to settle the final tax.

breakdown: IMT transfer tax 0-8% (progressive) + stamp duty 0.8% + notary/registry 0.9-1.2% + legal 1.25-2%.
annual_property_tax: IMI 0.3-0.45% of taxable value (urban), set by municipality.
rental_income_tax: Long-term: 25% flat for non-residents; short-term (AL) under the simplified regime only 35-50% of gross is taxable.

breakdown: Transfer taxes (droits de mutation) of about 5.8%, or about 6.3% in departments that raised their rate for 2025 to March 2028; notary fee (émoluments) on a sliding scale from 3.87% down to 0.799% plus 20% VAT, about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; land security contribution (contribution de sécurité immobilière) 0.10%; disbursements (débours) of about €800 to €1,200; the agent fee is usually built into the advertised price (FAI) and paid by the seller, sometimes shared.
annual_property_tax: Owners pay an annual property tax (taxe foncière) set by the local authorities, and owners of a furnished second home also pay housing tax (taxe d'habitation), which some communes raise by a surcharge of 5% to 60%.
rental_income_tax: Non-residents pay French income tax on French rental income at a minimum rate of 20% (30% above about €27,500), plus social charges of 17.2%, or 7.5% for people covered by social security in another EU/EEA country or Switzerland.

breakdown: Registration tax 9% on a second home (resale), or VAT on new builds; notary 1-2% + legal ~1% + agent ~3% (GPG roundtrip 10-18%).
annual_property_tax: IMU 0.4-1.06% on second homes (on cadastral value).
rental_income_tax: Optional flat 'cedolare secca' on short lets: 21% for one property, 26% from the second.

breakdown: New build: 10% IVA + 0.5-1.5% AJD stamp duty + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-2%; resale: ITP transfer tax 6-11% instead of IVA/AJD.
annual_property_tax: IBI 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value (municipal), plus imputed income tax on unlet homes.
rental_income_tax: Non-residents: EU/EEA 19% on net income; non-EU 24% on gross with no deductions.

breakdown: BPHTB transfer tax 5% + notary 1-2.5% + legal 0.5-1.5% (GPG: 6.5-9%); new developer units add 11% PPN/VAT (stack ~17-18% without the 2026 PPN-DTP incentive, ~6-9% with it). Plain leasehold deals mostly notary/legal.
annual_property_tax: PBB land & building tax, up to ~0.5% of assessed NJOP-based value (low hundreds USD on a $300k villa).
rental_income_tax: Non-residents: 20% withholding on gross rent (10% possible under a tax treaty); PT PMA companies 22% corporate tax.

breakdown: BPHTB 5% + notary 1-2.5% + legal 0.5-1.5%; +11% PPN/VAT on new developer units unless the 2026 VAT incentive applies.
annual_property_tax: PBB, up to ~0.5% of assessed (NJOP-based) value.
rental_income_tax: Non-residents: 20% withholding on gross rent (10% possible under a treaty); PT PMA 22% corporate tax.

breakdown: Title deed transfer fee for foreigners 6-12% (sources disagree: 9% most cited, 12% in one 2026 guide) + 5% VAT on new builds (one source says 19%) + 0.5% stamp duty + legal GBP 1,000-2,500 + transformer fee GBP 1,500-3,000 on new builds.
annual_property_tax: Per m2, very low: about GBP 10-100/yr for a typical apartment or villa.
rental_income_tax: 10% of gross rental income (Investra, 2026).
